sentences.text: Fossils from Scotland reveal an eel-shaped animal up to 6 cm long with a skull of hardened cartilage.
This skull featured nasal and auditory capsules, a gill apparatus, and ambiguous jaw structures.
A fossilized braincase of P. australis revealed that the animal lacked a postorbital process and an intracranial joint.
The genus Palaeospondylus was first described by Traquair in 1890.

Scientific understanding of its identity has varied, with a 2004 suggestion that it was a larval lungfish, a 2017 proposal that it was a stem chondrichthyan, and a current classification under the class Chondrichthyes.
Palaeospondylus lived approximately 400 to 390 million years ago during the Early and Middle Devonian epochs.
Fossils of this genus have been found in Scotland and Australia.
